name: mock-browser-window

frames.best_why: All frames are nearly identical; frame 1 shows the full window, sidebar and dashboard without a cursor.

tagline: A dark browser window frames a small analytics dashboard.
summary: A rounded mock app window with three macOS dots, a URL bar and a left sidebar, holding a demo dashboard of three stat cards and a bar chart. It is a frame; the sidebar and content come from props and children.
appearance: A dark rounded window with a thin border. The top row has three small traffic-light dots on the left and a pill-shaped URL bar in the centre. A narrow left sidebar lists five items, the first tinted as active, beside three small stat cards and a row of grey bars.
behaviour: Static: nothing moves or responds. The URL, sidebar items and inner content are supplied by props and children, but the frame itself has no interaction.
demo_content: Sidebar Overview, Analytics, Customers, Billing, Settings; stat cards over a bar chart.
search_phrases: app mockup with a url bar
frame for a landing page screenshot
use_when: You want to frame a dashboard screenshot as a believable app window on a marketing page.
avoid_when: Real navigation is needed: this is a static frame whose dots and links do nothing.
customise: size, variant, headerStyle, url, showSidebar, sidebarPosition, sidebarItems and theme are props; the window content is children. The theme prop currently has no effect.
weight_why: A few nested divs and one inline SVG; no images, scripts or motion.

a11y.note: Traffic dots and sidebar rows look clickable but are plain divs with no handlers or keyboard access.

props.name: sidebarItems
props.type: Array<{ icon?: React.ReactNode; label: string; active?: boolean; badge?: string | number }>

issues: The theme prop is accepted but all three values resolve to the same classes, so it does nothing.
The traffic lights and sidebar rows look clickable but have no behaviour.
polish_why: Crisp window chrome and tidy dashboard demo; the dead theme prop and fake controls are small flaws.
